thread:
jamal: heads up — after the 13.2 kernel + nvidia-driver 535.86 roll in us-west, a bunch of multi-gpu jobs are falling back to NET sockets for peer comms and throughput is tanking (~3-4x).
mina: :eyes: any logs or nccl output you can paste? is this on mixed H100/A100 racks or a single SKU?
jamal: mostly mixed racks (H100 + A100). quick snippet from a failing job:
jamal: ```
NCCL WARN NET/Socket transport fallback for 1 peer(s)
NCCL INFO Using socket for rank 2 -> rank 3, fallback reason: p2pStatus=UNSUPPORTED
NCCL ERROR Timeout while waiting for epoll on socket
``` 
ryan: do we have nvidia-smi topo -m from both node types? that usually makes the mismatch obvious.
jamal: pasted two outputs — H100 node:
jamal: ```
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity
GPU0     X      CPU-0
GPU1    PIX0     X     CPU-1
``` 
jamal: and A100 node shows NVLink pairs as expected.
lucy: that H100 topo looks wrong, nvlink links aren't showing. could be the kernel/userdriver interface broke NVLINK reporting after the kernel upgrade.
mina: also check /dev/shm perms and nvidia-persistenced, sometimes SHM-created sockets fail and nccl falls back to socket transport.
ryan: run on a repro node: 
ryan: ```bash
# check driver/kernel
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
uname -a
modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic
# check topo
nvidia-smi topo -m
# check nvlink presence
dmesg | grep -i nvlink
# nccl debug
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
mpirun -np 4 python run_allreduce.py
``` 
jamal: dmesg on H100 shows repeated: "nvlink: failed to initialize peer mapping for device 1" and a few WARNs about iommu.
lucy: I vaguely remember a kernel change that flipped the IOMMU driver ordering on some kernels; that can break peer mapping when the nvidia module probes before the peer-memory / nvidia-uvm services are ready.
mina: infra-bot, can you roll back the driver on a single affected node to the previous 535.65 and run the same repro? @infra-bot
infra-bot: scheduled action: rollback-driver(535.86 -> 535.65) on node us-west-3a-gpu-07 in queue. ETA ~12m. :gear:
ryan: if rollback fixes it then we'll know it's the driver/kernel interplay. if not, it might be NCCL detection sensitivity — we had a patch in nccl 2.18 that relaxed peer checks.
jamal: after rollback (quick test): NVLink appears again in topo and same workload latency drops back to expected range. so far looks like driver/kernel combo.
lucy: ok plan: 1) hold further 535.86 rolls in west; 2) run a node-level canary with extra nvlink/ip checks; 3) open bug with driver vendor + uplink kernel tags; 4) add a healthcheck to our rollout pipeline that fails if nvidia-smi topo doesn't show >=1 NVLink pair for GPU family nodes.
mina: can we also add an automated NCCL transport histogram to console so we catch socket fallbacks early? even a burn-rate alert if NET tokens > 5% of tokens.
ryan: yes — Redwood Console: we can add per-cluster metric nccl.transport.counts{socket,shm,net} by model route. I'll open the ticket.
jamal: created quick PR to rollback policy and a healthcheck script gist: ```
#!/bin/bash
OUT=$(nvidia-smi topo -m)
if echo "$OUT" | grep -q "PX"; then
  echo OK
  exit 0
else
  echo FAIL
  exit 1
fi
``` 
lucy: thanks. add to rollout gate and notify the firmware/driver vendor with kernel version and dmesg log. tagging this as blocker for further 535.86 expansion. :hammer:
mina: adding followup: check /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/nvlink_remote_* files too, sometimes the sysfs nodes move after a reprobe.
infra-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026 - p2p peermap regression after 13.2 + driver 535.86; affected: us-west gpu racks; mitigation: rollback on queued nodes; followups assigned to jamal, ryan, lucy.
